neighbours.label: the token ' in' (also ' on') used as a locative or temporal preposition after a verb phrase
fire: The subject came up in a meeting with the board.
Sales started to recover in 1952 after the strike.
A red sticker in the corner of the window marks the car.
The issue was raised in parliament last spring.
Protesters marched in the streets of the capital.
Prices began to rise in March of that year.
The fish were kept in a tank near the door.
Her name appeared in the local paper twice.
quiet: The subject came up during a meeting with the board.
Sales started to recover after 1952 following the strike.
A red sticker near the corner of the window marks the car.
The issue was raised by parliament last spring.
Protesters marched through the streets of the capital.
Prices began to rise by March of that year.
The fish were kept beside a tank near the door.
Her name appeared beside the local paper's logo twice.

notes: card flags this pole broad; the opposite pole also peaks on ' in', so the + side may need a specific construction
